practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string only from an environment variable or secret store (DOCUMENTDB_URI); never hard-code credentials or commit them, and provide a .env.example placeholder for developers.
practices.prior_belief: Read the database connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secrets store; do not hard-code credentials in source or commit them. Use a .env.example with a placeholder but never commit the real URI.

practices.practice: Create a single, process-level MongoClient / Mongoose connection and reuse it across the app (singleton pattern); configure the connection pool (e.g., maxPoolSize) according to workload rather than opening a new connection per request.
practices.prior_belief: Reuse a single Mongoose/MongoDB connection across the app and configure connection pooling (set maxPoolSize in the connection string or options). Do not open a new connection per request.

practices.practice: Require TLS and lock down network access: always connect with TLS (tls=true), avoid disabling certificate validation in production, and restrict access using firewall rules or Private Endpoints (prefer VNet/private endpoint and least-privilege identities).
practices.prior_belief: Lock down network access to the cluster: require TLS (tls=true in the connection string), restrict by IP firewall or use private endpoints/VNet integration, and avoid exposing DB admin ports publicly.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document ACID transactions (use startSession()/withTransaction and pass the session to each operation) and transactions may span collections and shards; use the driver's transaction APIs to commit or retry.
practices.prior_belief: For multi-document transactions, always start the transaction on a session from the same client/connection and ensure the involved collections are in the same database and appropriate partition/shard so the transaction is supported; keep transactions short and touch as few documents as possible.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: When using transactions, run them with the driver's withTransaction helper (or equivalent), avoid non-idempotent external side effects inside the transaction callback, and keep transaction scope small so retries and auto-retries are safe.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Pick the shard/partition key to collocate related data: for read-heavy workloads choose the most common query filter (to localize reads); for write-heavy workloads choose a high-cardinality evenly distributed key to avoid hot partitions.
practices.prior_belief: Choose the partition / shard key (Mongo shardKey or Cosmos partitionKey equivalent) to collocate account's events and balance documents (e.g., accountId). This reduces cross-partition transactions and improves performance.

practices.practice: Create a compound index on (accountId, timestamp) (accountId ascending, timestamp descending if queries return most-recent-first) to support efficient /history queries that page by time.
practices.prior_belief: Create an index on (accountId, timestamp) or (partitionKey, timestamp) to support efficient /history queries that page by time; make it a descending timestamp index if queries request recent events first.

practices.practice: Create a unique index on balances.accountId (one balance document per account) and update that document atomically inside the same transaction that inserts the event, rather than rebuilding balances from events on every read.
practices.prior_belief: Create a unique index on balances.accountId and always update balances with an atomic update (inside transactions) rather than rebuilding from events on every read.

practices.practice: Make index creation idempotent in startup/seed scripts (call createIndexes and tolerate already-exists), and avoid blocking the application on long foreground index builds when possible.
practices.prior_belief: Make index creation idempotent in startup/seed scripts: call createIndexes and tolerate 'already exists' errors; avoid blocking operations at app startup by creating indexes ahead of traffic and/or in background where supported.

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') / the profiler and index-stats to verify /history and aggregation queries use the intended indexes; iterate on index shape when explain shows a COLLSCAN or blocking SORT.
practices.prior_belief: Use the database profiler and explain plans (the MCP tools or driver explain()) to verify that /history and aggregation queries use the intended indexes; iterate on indexes when explain shows COLLSCAN on hot queries.

practices.practice: Use idempotency/deduplication keys and enforce them with a uniqueness constraint (or transactional marker) so retries and duplicate deliveries are safe; record the deduplication key and the business write in the same transaction when possible.
practices.prior_belief: Use an idempotency key on events (unique index on idempotencyKey) to make seeding and client retries safe and to prevent duplicate events when clients retry due to timeouts.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB idempotency unique index retry duplicate prevention

practices.practice: Denormalize and precompute read-heavy aggregates (e.g., maintain a small balances document with lifetime totals) to avoid running full-collection aggregation scans per request, or ensure aggregations are selective and backed by indexes.
practices.prior_belief: For aggregation-based tier/status calculations (lifetime points), either precompute lifetime totals on the balances document or ensure the $group match stage is selective and backed by an index (e.g., accountId). Avoid full-collection scans for each request.

practices.practice: Avoid unbounded arrays and large binary/blobs inside documents; keep documents well under the 16 MB BSON limit and split large fields into side collections or blob storage if needed.
practices.prior_belief: Do not store unbounded arrays or large attachments inside event documents; if you need large blobs, store them in a blob store and reference them in the event document to keep BSON size under limits and queries fast.

practices.practice: Enable retryable reads/writes and implement bounded application retry logic with exponential backoff; design writes to be idempotent so retries are safe and consider driver retry settings (retryReads/retryWrites) as part of the strategy.
practices.prior_belief: Enable retryable writes and implement retry logic for transactions using MongoDB error labels (TransientTransactionError, UnknownTransactionCommitResult) with exponential backoff. Keep retries bounded and idempotent via idempotency keys or unique constraints.

practices.practice: When using vector search, define fixed vector dimensionality, choose the right index type for scale (DiskANN for large sets, HNSW/IVF for smaller), tune build/search params, and normalize embeddings for cosine similarity before storing.

Provision cluster compute and storage separately: pick Premium SSD v2 for new clusters, size storage for capacity and choose the compute tier to meet IOPS/bandwidth (IOPS are gated by compute tier, not disk size).
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput appropriately (RU/s or autoscale) for the collections that will receive writes (events and balances), and monitor consumed RU to avoid throttling. Use separate collections for write-heavy and read-heavy workloads if necessary.

practices.practice: Use the Azure guidance for idempotent operations and transactional outbox/inbox patterns when writing seed/verification scripts so they are safe to rerun (use upserts, existence checks, or create-if-missing inside a transaction or idempotent workflow).
practices.prior_belief: For seed and verification scripts, write them to be idempotent (use upserts or check-and-create) and run them under developer control; do not assume seeding will be re-run safely without idempotency protections.

practices.practice: Use monitoring and diagnostics: enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs, ingest them into Log Analytics, and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation for the cluster tier.
Prefer the service text/vector search features (textSearch / $search) over community $text indexes for production text search workloads on Azure DocumentDB.
Keep transactions small and short-lived (touch as few documents as possible), and be prepared to retry or abort and retry transactions that hit conflicts or time limits.
practices.prior_belief: Keep transactions and write operations under size limits: avoid modifying many documents in one transaction and avoid very large documents; prefer updating a balances document and inserting a single event per transaction rather than bulk-modifying many rows.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Do not assume driver writeConcern settings (w, j) will be honored identically across services; if strong durability guarantees are required, verify the service's behavior and documentation for write concern mapping before relying on w:'majority' or j:true.
practices.prior_belief: Set write concern to ensure durability for ledger operations (use w: 'majority' and j: true where supported) and verify the provider honors those write concerns; do not rely on default acknowledged writes for financial/ledger integrity without checking.
practices.how_found: search: Azure DocumentDB write concern w majority j; search: Azure DocumentDB durability writeConcern; search: 'writeConcern' site:learn.microsoft.com azure documentdb

practices.practice: Some Mongoose-specific client optimizations (e.g., using .lean() for read-heavy queries and projecting only required fields) are general MongoDB best practices but are not explicitly documented in Azure DocumentDB guidance; treat them as application-level optimizations to apply when using Mongoose.
practices.prior_belief: When using Mongoose for read-heavy endpoints, use .lean() on queries that return plain JSON and avoid large document population unless needed; prefer projections to return only required fields (e.g., event type, amount, timestamp) for /history and /balance endpoints.
practices.how_found: search: Mongoose .lean() Azure DocumentDB; search: 'lean()' site:learn.microsoft.com 'DocumentDB' 'Mongoose'

notes:
I discovered public guidance across the installed DocumentDB skills (connection, driver, indexing, data-modeling, sharding, security, storage, monitoring, vector-search) and Microsoft Learn docs. Practices implemented in the sample (env var for DOCUMENTDB_URI, singleton connection, transactions, append-only events + balances, createIndexes usage, .lean() usage in code) align with many public recommendations. Two prior beliefs lacked an explicit Azure DocumentDB documentation confirmation in the public sources searched: write-concern (w/j) specifics and a Mongoose .lean() recommendation — these remain 'prior_knowledge_only'. K03 (transactions must be limited to same DB/partition) and K14 (provision RU/s autoscale) were contradicted by Azure DocumentDB public guidance (Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document ACID transactions across collections/shards and uses compute tiers + Premium SSD v2 rather than RU/sec autoscale).

Prior beliefs the discovery step did not classify: K04, K20. See 05a-prior-beliefs.json.
